metadata.task_name: OIDC Auth Flow and Session Token Handling

execution.coverage: 100% — all four target files read and all OIDC code paths traced

finding.preliminary_assessment: The VULN-007 fix validates redirectUri using new URL(res.redirectUri) and checks parsed.protocol !== 'https:'. However, protocol-relative URLs (//evil.com) are a known bypass: when a URL begins with '//', the URL constructor inherits the protocol from the current document's location. If the application is served over HTTPS (as expected in production), new URL('//evil.com') returns protocol='https:' — the scheme check passes. The redirect then navigates window.location.href to the attacker-controlled IdP, which can accept the OIDC code exchange, steal the authorization code, and issue malicious tokens. This requires a compromised ApplinX REST server to supply a malicious redirectUri. The fix comment VULN-007 describes 'URL constructor validates scheme' but does not account for protocol inheritance in protocol-relative URLs.

patterns_observed: State nonce correctly generated (crypto.randomUUID()) and stored BEFORE redirect — GOOD
Authorization code NOT stored in sessionStorage (VULN-009 correct) — GOOD
Token cleared on logout (setNotConnected removes gx_token, idPcode, userName) — GOOD
URL scheme check present (VULN-007) but bypassed by protocol-relative URLs — BAD
Username stored in sessionStorage as JSON-stringified value — exposure risk on XSS
Authorization code appears in queryParams passed to /instant route — may be in browser history

false_positives.rationale: Unsafe JSON.parse without try-catch is a DoS risk, not an authentication issue — flagged separately in R-M-001
State is a UUID, properly encoded — not a bypass
Requires further investigation of /instant route behavior but is not confirmed as a code injection bypass

analysis.coverage_assessment: Complete — all four target files analyzed. Full OIDC flow traced: nonce generation, IdP redirect, callback validation, code exchange, token storage, logout cleanup. Multiple issues identified in addition to primary finding.

for_inquisitor: Test protocol-relative URL bypass: supply redirectUri='//evil.com/auth' and verify if new URL('//evil.com/auth') returns https: protocol when called on HTTPS page
Verify if the redirect URL can reach an attacker-controlled IdP that would accept the OIDC code
Assess: add hostname allowlist validation or verify redirectUri must match a pre-registered IdP hostname
Examine /instant route: does it re-execute code exchange? Is the authorization code in queryParams persisted in browser history?
Verify username sessionStorage exposure — is there a path where this.user value leads to privilege escalation?
